study_design: Prospective matched case-control analysis with 254 prostate cancer cases and 514 matched controls.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: We related plasma levels of these factors to prostate cancer risk in a prospective study of 254 case subjects and 514 matched control subjects.
reason: The abstract prospectively analyzes overall prostate cancer risk. It does not present an incident aggressive prostate cancer analysis; indexing terms concerning metastasis do not establish such an endpoint in the abstract.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: After adjustment for the other 2 plasma variables, body mass index and smoking, a statistically significant increased risk remained only for vitamin B12 (OR = 2.96; 95% CI = 1.58-5.55; p(trend) = 0.001).
estimate_classifications.reason: The vitamin B12 estimate is reported for overall prostate cancer risk, without an aggressive disease definition.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Adjusted OR for folate and homocysteine were 1.30 (95% CI = 0.74-2.24; p(trend) = 0.17) and 0.91 (95% CI = 0.51-1.58; p(trend) = 0.60), respectively.
estimate_classifications.reason: The folate estimate is reported for overall prostate cancer risk, without an aggressive disease definition.

validation_findings: Nested case-control/case-cohort analytic denominator must not be forced to full-cohort N
